stops.name: Puente Nuevo
stops.detail: The Puente Nuevo (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈpwente ˈnweβo], "New Bridge"), completed in 1793, is the newest and largest of three bridges that span the 120-metre-deep (390 ft) chasm, the El Tajo Gorge, that carries the Guadalevín River and divides the city of Ronda, in southern Spain. The architect was José Martin de Aldehuela and the chief builder was Juan Antonio Díaz Machuca.
